cands.name: Todd Delmay
cands.bio: Democratic nominee for HD 101. Hollywood businessman and executive director of SAVE, an LGBTQ civil rights organization; he and his husband were plaintiffs in the Florida marriage-equality case. Lost the 2022 HD 101 primary to Cassel, 34% to 40%.

record.text: Has not held elected office. Former president of Dolphin Democrats and past chair of the Prideline board.

money_notes.text: Spent $165,000 from his campaign through Oct. 9 with $28,000 in in-kind help from the Florida Democratic Party and House Democratic Campaign Committee; raised another $140,000 in his Delmay for Florida PC.

endorsements.text: South Florida Sun-Sentinel editorial board; Broward Teachers Union; Florida Education Association; AFSCME Florida; Florida AFL-CIO; SEIU Florida; Planned Parenthood; U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz; Broward Jewish Democratic Caucus.

cands.name: Hillary Cassel
cands.bio: Republican state representative for HD 101 since 2022; attorney (Cassel & Cassel, founded 2017) and former assistant state attorney. Elected as a Democrat; left the Democratic Party for the GOP on Dec. 27, 2024, citing the party's stance on Israel.
cands.local_ties: Born in Boynton Beach; HD 101 spans Hallandale Beach to Dania Beach and Davie (residence not stated in sources).

record.text: Voted in January 2026 for a bill expanding Florida's Wrongful Death Act to cover fetuses at any stage; it passed the House on party lines and died in the Senate. She said it was not about abortion. Her site emphasizes her prosecutor record and district appropriations.

money_notes.text: Campaign spent $202,000 through Oct. 2 and reported $177,000 in assistance from the Republican Party of Florida and the Florida House Republican Campaign Committee; her Balanced Leadership political committee spent another $388,000.

controversies.text: Democrats, including opponent Todd Delmay, accuse her of betraying the voters who elected her as a Democrat; she says she has remained consistent on LGBTQ rights and abortion access.
